analysis: The broad option links sociological theory, qualitative inquiry and empirical methods to inequality, media, health and institutions. It uses the full available five-course sociology spine.

The work option retains that spine and makes workplaces and policy a sustained focus through organisational psychology, negotiation, public economics and econometrics. Gender history and social psychology add institutional and group context.

The crime and safety option brings social theory and collective action together with criminal justice, social institutions, youth resilience, conflict and evidence synthesis. It does not claim a digital forensics or specialist cybercrime sequence. Each option directly studies sociology and applies it to a distinct set of questions.

ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, evidence literacy, presentation and reflective development support the common foundation; this is common academic and civic formation.

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice

GOSHIST112.name: Histories of Gender

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy

GOSLAWJ211.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: compares public institutions, constitutional rights and judicial oversight across systems

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: uses political theory to examine authority, institutions, rights and justice

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: uses classical and critical sociological theory to examine inequality, networks, migration and institutions

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops interviews, focus groups, observation, reflexivity and qualitative analysis

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: examines contemporary social theory and critical approaches to modernity and exclusion

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: applies social-movement theory to mobilisation and environmental justice cases

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: uses contemporary social theories to analyse civil society, hegemony, social capital and trust

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: applies epidemiological designs to health patterns and social determinants in a local project

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces psychological and neuroscientific foundations for later study of behaviour and development

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: studies influence, prejudice, group processes and behaviour in social settings

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: uses experimental design and multivariable statistical models to investigate human behaviour

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: synthesises research on behavioural and related questions through systematic review and meta-analysis

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: studies development and contextual influences on behaviour and social relationships over the lifespan

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: examines youth radicalisation and educational prevention through belonging, risk and resilience

MCCCOMM213.name: Rhetoric in Action
MCCCOMM213.contribution: develops audience-aware speaking and teaching through a community project with primary-school children

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: applies evidence on framing, social influence and ethical persuasion in public communication projects

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.contribution: examines racial representation, power and resistance in US cultural history and develops a research-based podcast

academicConstruction: Economics moves to the first term in both affected options, and Comparative Politics takes the vacated terms. Rhetoric in Action swaps with Data Science in option two. Human Rights swaps with Criminal Law in option three, which also adds Social Movements & Environmental Justice in place of Psychopathology to strengthen the sociology spine. Seven, six and seven advanced courses remain. Pairwise differences are eight, eight and ten courses each way. None of the options claims dedicated social network analysis, specialist labour sociology or the same project-and-thesis sequence.
